resources.string: One sentence about what it does.
Each chip is one moment of the move. Drag to move it or stretch it.
How high the Imp jumps in this beat.
The picture shown for this move in lists.
A name so you can find it again.
Squash or stretch the body, like a ball.
A small picture that pops up beside the Imp.
How far the Imp leans to the side.
Set up The Den to find more.
Open Imp when you sign in.
How big the window is. You can still drag its edges.
That picture could not be used. Pick another one.
A tile repeats to fill the window. Pick a seamless pattern.
A secret password that lets the Imp use this service. It stays on this Mac.
The exact brain of the service. Bigger ones think better but are slower.
Pick who does the thinking for this Imp.
Use the Brain every Imp shares, or pick a different one just for this Imp.
A Brain is a service and a model. %1$s thinks with it.
No Brains yet. Add a model on this computer or a service with your key.
Pick what kind of thing to look for.
Anyone can add it. Chats, memory and keys are never included.
Type a word to find things.
Where people share Imps, animations, triggers and tools.
A short name for the web address. Use small letters and dashes.
Show the most loved first, or the newest first.
One sentence so people know what it is.
Words that help people find it. Separate them with commas.
For a device that can\'t scan: paste the link in Scan code on the other device. Keep it private. It lets a device link with this Mac for a while.
No devices yet. Link an iPhone or another Mac and your Imps can visit it.
Devices linked with this one. Mine lets a device act for you.
Link another device here. The dot shows whether The Hop lets devices find each other from anywhere.
%1$s did not accept the key. Check it and try again.
No model answered. Make sure it is running, then try again.
%1$s does not have the model %2$s. Pick another one.
%1$s has no Brain yet, so it cannot answer.
No network. Check your connection, then try again.
%1$s did not answer in time. Check its address, or try again later.
Cannot reach %1$s. Check the address and your connection.
Could not save that. Check the free space and try again.
Could not share %1$s. Try again in a moment.
%1$s could not start. Check its settings.
When Imp reads a page or looks for something on one, it shows up here.
Lets Imp know which page you are on and where things are on it. Talks only to Imp on this computer.
Start Imp on this computer and this connects by itself.
Opens the Imp app. It starts Imp if it is not running.
Looks for Imp again. Use it after you start Imp.
The browser keeps this page to itself. Imp only knows its address.
Imp can read this page and find things on it when it needs to.
%1$s is asleep. Give it a Brain to wake it up.
That address does not look right. It starts with https:// or http://.
Imp could not save the key. Try again.
Use the address of your computer on this network.
Any OpenAI-compatible API. Your key stays on this device.
Its look, Brain settings, tools, triggers and chats go with it. This can\'t be undone.
Imps move around here. Press Tab to go from one Imp to the next.
Hatch your first Imp to get started.
Hidden Imps peek out now and then. Click one to bring it back.
%1$s is peeking out from the floor.
It comes back here now, even if %1$s is gone for good. If %1$s connects again, it learns the Imp left.
Drag it out of the window to let it out.
This desktop does not let apps place free windows, so Imps stay in the window.
%2$s did not take %1$s. It stays here.
%1$s is asleep. Give it a Brain.
Also copy what this Imp talked about.
Paste a kit, a web address or an imp:// link, or drop a file. You look at it first.
Things in the kit this Mac cannot use, so they are left out.
Tools can run things on your Mac. Read them first.
Local Network is off for Imp
Imp couldn\'t read its saved links, so it started fresh. Link your devices again.
Small traits that change how %1$s moves and looks around.
Pick the colour and the size of this Imp.
Tilt the eyebrows. One way looks cross, the other looks sad.
Small touches that change the face and the way it moves.
The colour of this Imp. Drag along the strip to change it.
Make the eyes smaller or bigger.
Tilt the head to one side or the other.
Turn the horns up or down.
How closed the eyelids are. More makes it look sleepy.
How quickly it does everything. 1.0 is normal.
How big this Imp is on your screen.
Squeeze the eyes tight, or open them wide.
How big a chat gets before the Imp suggests a recap or a new chat.
How many of the latest messages go to the Brain with each one. Fewer is faster and cheaper.
Also sends what the tools did and returned. Off is smaller and cheaper.
Hide the Imps on your desktop
No Imps are out on the desktop
Pick one of the moves every Imp has and make a version only for this Imp.
Choose what this Imp does when you move your mouse pointer: stay still, look at it, or run after it.
Off: it stays still. Eyes: only its eyes look at the pointer. Hop: it jumps after the pointer. Glide: it slides after the pointer.
Moves made for only this Imp. They play instead of the shared ones.
How fast it goes after the pointer. Only for Hop and Glide.
Researching on the web, fixing code…
One or two lines. The other Imps read it to know whom to ask for what.
What you call this Imp. Say its name and it answers.
Tell it who to be, like a kind pirate or a quiet helper. It will talk that way.
The hidden rules that tell it how to answer. Most people never change them.
What shows on your screen while this Imp talks out loud.
Pick the picture shown while it talks: Glow is a glowing edge, Smoke is a puff of smoke, Both shows the two, Players is a small player with play and pause.
Part of who %1$s is. You can change it any time.
Tell %1$s who it is and how it talks.
The first model that chats, chosen when it wakes.
Imps you hatch on this iPhone show here, each with the Brain it thinks with.
Starts a message asking %1$s to do something.
Its Imps come home. To link again, show a new code.
Every Imp comes home. Link again with a new code.
Taps in your hand when you pick something, when an Imp comes or goes, and when something works or fails.
Imp switches language the next time it opens.
Devices linked with this iPhone. Imps can travel between you.
The clipboard doesn\'t hold a link from Imp.
Copy the link from the other device first, then paste it here.
That isn\'t a link from Imp.
Scan the code on the other device
Other devices see this iPhone by this name.
Who is this Imp? How does it talk?
Each rest is this many times longer than the one before.
How long the Imp rests before it asks again.
How long an Imp waits for its Brain, and what it does when the internet drops.
How many times the Imp asks again when the internet drops. Wrong keys are never tried again.
If the Brain takes longer than this, the Imp stops waiting and says so.
Shake the iPhone next to a linked device and the Imp you moved last goes there. You can undo it.
Its chats and keys are forgotten. This can\'t be undone.
%1$s moves in on %2$s for good, and its key goes with it. %2$s asks you to look it over first.
Throw an Imp off the side of another screen. It lands here.
Bring Imps over from your Mac or another iPhone.
A tiny helper that lives on your screen and thinks with the AI you choose.
Paste a key from an AI service, or use a model on your Mac.
Lets an Imp run commands on this computer when you ask.
Used only when you talk to an Imp by voice.
Only for your own devices. Their Imps may use tools on this one.
Where Imps share animations, triggers and Imps. Shared items are public.
This needs a Den. Set one in Settings.
Sharing and finding in The Den are off.
Lets your devices find each other. It only passes encrypted data.
Linking from anywhere needs a Hop. Add one in Settings under Devices. Devices on the same network still find each other.
Only devices on the same network find each other.
The default, run by the Imp project.
Cannot reach it. Check the address.
%1$s isn\'t running on this computer. Start it first.
Text, icons and switches on coloured buttons are white or black. A colour too light or too dark for them is shown a shade deeper or lighter.
How the app starts and which language it speaks.
The Den is not set up.
The Hop is not set up.
Save your Imps and settings in a file, or load them back.
Erase everything and begin again. This cannot be undone.
How long to wait before asking again.
Keep keys safe in your Mac\'s Keychain.
How much longer each pause gets.
How patient an Imp is when a brain is slow.
How many times to ask again if it fails.
The brains your Imps think with.
How long to wait for an answer before giving up.
How much of the desktop shows through the bubble.
What shows while a voice or sound plays.
Plays a picture, video or sound in a reply as soon as it arrives.
Whether the bubble is solid or lets what is behind it show through.
How long a bubble stays after the Imp stops talking.
How many lines the text box grows to before it scrolls.
What the bubble does with sound and video.
Preview of the bubble on a light, a dark and a busy background
The size of the chat bubble. Drag its corner to change it.
Link another device so your Imps can visit it.
On for your own devices, off for a friend\'s

Turn on for a device that\'s yours. Its Imps can then message the Imps here, Imps answer it with their tools, it can open any Imp\'s files, and an Imp you throw to it goes without asking. Turn it on on both devices so Imps talk both ways. Leave it off for a friend\'s device: Imps still answer it, but without tools.
Its tools can be used from here
So Imp can press keys and click for you.
What your Mac lets Imp do.
The web address of the brain.
A brain on the internet. It may ask for a key.
A secret password the brain asks for.
A brain that runs on this computer.
A name you pick for this brain.
How Imps talk to each other.
The language you speak to it. It listens in this one.
Which chat a message from one Imp to another lands in.
Whether Imps keep chatting in the same chat or start a new one.
Whether an Imp waits for the answer of the Imp it messages, or goes on and hears it later as a new turn.
How many minutes a chat stays the same chat.
The web address of the tool.
The command that starts the tool.
Extra lines sent with each request, like a password.
A name you pick for this tool.
Secret values the tool needs to run.
Set up The Den to share there.
Its look, personality, tools and triggers are shared. Keys, memory and chats never are.
Find animations, triggers and Imps others shared, or bring in a kit you have. To share yours, use the share button on an Imp.
The link to %1$s dropped. It reconnects on its own.
%1$s cannot reach its Brain. It wakes up when you are back online.
Imps that use a model on this device still work. The others wait until you are back online.
With no Brain, it cannot think. Its triggers still work.
%1$s is asleep because %2$s is not connected.
No tools yet. Add some from a kit or an MCP server.
Lets the Imp look at pages and use the browser you opened for it.
Things the Imp can already do, like look at your screen. Switch off any it should not use.
Extra tools added from outside. Each one gives the Imp new things to do.
A program or website that gives the Imp more tools.
What the Imp can do by itself. Switch off what it shouldn\'t use.
The Imp loses the tools of this server.
Every Imp that uses this tool gets this setup. Each Imp switches it on or off for itself.
No triggers yet. Add one and %1$s acts on its own.
What the Imp does when it goes off.
Which Imp does the job. A change here is for this Imp alone unless you pick Every Imp.
What the Imp gets to look at when it goes off, like the clipboard.
Tell the Imp in your own words what to do.
A trigger wakes the Imp up by itself when something happens, like a time or a low battery.
A name so you can find it again.
The triggers Imp comes with: clicks, falling asleep and waking up. You see them before anything is added.
What has to happen to set it off, like a time, an app or a low battery.
Saves a version for %1$s only. The other Imps keep the shared one.
A voice an Imp marks to play starts by itself in a new reply. Otherwise you tap it.
